A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic coverage experiments, MIMIC patient examples, prediction errors and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds original TCGA coverage and interval-width results, Gaussian-process results and synthetic interval-width measurements.

M1.justification: New Supplement A.3 provides bounded-error optimization for additive soft interventions on estimated propensities. This extends the existing procedures; the main algorithms and the fixed-Gaussian alternative already present in A.2 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Supplement C adds controlled semi-synthetic evaluation using TCGA gene-expression data from 9,659 patients and 4,000 features. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained scalar-confounder synthetic datasets and eight-confounder MIMIC application.

E2.justification: v3 adds an evaluated Gaussian-process regression comparator to the synthetic experiments, reporting its coverage and interval width in Section 5.2. MC dropout and deep ensembles were already evaluated in v2. The new TCGA tables report only the proposed method.

E3.justification: v3 adds interval width as a reported metric and introduces TCGA evaluation with shifts of 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5. Existing training budgets, synthetic sample counts and MIMIC splits remain unchanged. The main-text hard-intervention list changes to 7x and 10x, matching the already existing Table 1; this does not establish removal of an evaluated setting.

E4.justification: The existing intervention-strength plots, MIMIC case studies and runtime assessment are retained. The TCGA and interval-width tables expand benchmark and metric reporting. New passages about stability and varying M provide discussion or suggestions, without additional ablation, sensitivity or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Section 5.2 and the MSE table change their stated run counts from 10 to 50. However, v2's coverage-figure captions already specified 50 runs, and the MSE values remain identical. This establishes revised reporting, not a verified increase in executed runs. Mean-and-standard-deviation reporting already existed.

E6.justification: v3 adds TCGA coverage and width results in Tables 2–3, Gaussian-process results in Section 5.2, and synthetic width comparisons in Table 5. For example, dataset 2 at shift 10 has reported widths of 0.6711 for CP and 0.3235 for MC dropout. Table 1, the retained MSE table and empirical plots keep their previous results; the additions do not demonstrate same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem A.3 adds a coverage statement for soft interventions with estimated propensities, with a short reduction to existing theorems. Section 3 explicitly specifies Hölder smoothness, refining v2's appendix discussion of smoothness. The principal existing theorems and proofs are retained and renumbered.

C1.justification: The headline contributions remain finite-sample-valid, model-agnostic CP for continuous-treatment potential outcomes with estimated propensities, an interval-computation algorithm and empirical validation. The treatment-effect extension remains. Revised wording about validity guarantees does not change the stated coverage inequality.

C2.justification: Supplement E adds substantive discussions of unproved interval tightness, selecting M, the role of the propensity-error correction and instability under marginal coverage. Supplement F.4 explains lower coverage for a hard intervention through its position in the treatment-distribution tail. These considerably expand the interpretation and applicability qualifications beyond v2.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the CPU and memory, explains intervention selection and exclusion of treatments outside [0,40], and documents TCGA feature-selection and treatment-construction choices. These disclosures do not establish changes to existing preprocessing. The network, training, solver and code-access information is otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Figure 2 now acknowledge estimated-propensity finite-sample guarantees in the already cited Lei and Candès (2021). Supplement E.1 expands that comparison and explains the relationship to Gibbs et al. more explicitly. Additional citations support soft interventions, sensitivity parameters and TCGA, while the continuous-treatment research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v3 condenses and edits the narrative, moves Algorithm 1 and its discussion from Section 4.3 to Supplement B, expands explanations and reorganizes appendix subsections. Citation and cross-reference formatting changes throughout, but the main argumentative structure and much of the prose are retained.

P2.justification: Extensive reformatting relocates and enlarges Algorithm 1, rearranges existing figures, restructures Table 1 from dataset columns into grouped rows, and redraws Figure 2 with a separate Lei and Candès row. Three new result tables are added. The empirical plots themselves retain their content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, controlled high-dimensional TCGA evaluation, quantitative interval widths and clearer limitations make the evidence more informative. The method extension and revised prior-work discussion also help. The improvement is limited by incomplete TCGA protocol details and an overstated claim of consistently achieving coverage: Table 2 includes 0.7667 against a 0.8 target.
